mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 7% may signal economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with rising unemployment may indicate a late-cycle expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods with strong GDP and rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production may signal strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods with rising INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales may indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods with high RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates alongside low unemployment may indicate tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods with high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth during an expansion may lead to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods with rising PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts and retail sales during an expansion may indicate robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods with strong HOUST and RSAFS.
